comparison: Both evaluate claims C1, C4-C7, C10, C15 regarding behavioral sequence measures. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging data from multiple measures and appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising critical concerns about sequence variability, stereotypy, missing post-hoc analyses, and whether aged mice have a specific sequence deficit versus simply checking the magazine more frequently.

Both evaluate claims C2-C3 regarding overall instrumental performance. Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites the mixed ANOVA showing equivalent overall performance, and peer reviewers acknowledge that 'both young and aged mice significantly escalated their overall performance' without challenge.

Both evaluate claims C8-C9 regarding differential behavioral strategies in response to sequence trigger. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on significant training × age interaction. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether aged mice learned the contingency or showed behavioral inflexibility, requesting additional data on sequence trigger performance.

Both evaluate claims C11-C14 regarding sensory/perceptual controls. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, concluding the data rules out sensory confounds. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 raising critical concerns about hearing ability in aged C57 mice and requesting data to support or refute this possibility.

Both evaluate claims C16-C21 regarding lever hold task performance. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on significant training × age interaction with visual confirmation. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging these findings without raising specific concerns about methodology or interpretation.

Both evaluate acoustic analysis claims (C22-C27 for OpenEval; C22-C24, C26-C27 for peer review). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on statistical differences in speeds, intervals, and reward efficiency. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning the chunking analysis methodology and requesting quantitative methods beyond visual interpretation and proportional analyses.

Both evaluate claims C28-C37 regarding temporal analysis and boundary intervals. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive temporal analysis showing differential boundary interval patterns. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the data does not provide evidence of different chunking and may reflect different amounts of overall lever pressing, requesting quantitative methods.

Both evaluate claims C40-C46 regarding p-MAPK neuronal mapping. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on comprehensive mapping showing significant age × region interaction and correlation analyses. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising major concerns about confounds from general differences in lever pressing and questioning whether groups were matched for total presses.

Both evaluate claims C50-C61 regarding chemogenetic manipulation of DLS D1 MSNs. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting validated manipulation with significant effects while acknowledging incomplete phenocopy. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with all three reviewers expressing concerns that the manipulation does not recapitulate the full aging phenotype and questioning the high CNO dose and repeated dosing effects.

Both evaluate claims C63-C73 regarding feedback cue removal experiment. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on significant drops in sequence measures with cue removal and visual evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising alternative interpretations that the auditory cue may act as a conditioned reinforcer rather than action feedback, and linking effects to potential hearing deficits.

OpenEval evaluates claims C38, C47-C49, C74-C81, C86-C87, C89-C90, C92-C93, C100-C105 regarding literature citations, finding them SUPPORTED as accurate and relevant. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these citation-based claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C82-C85, C88, C94-C97 regarding interpretations and conclusions, finding them SUPPORTED as appropriately qualified and logically following from evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluates claim C62 regarding citation of Lindenberger and Mayr (2014), finding it SUPPORTED as accurate attribution. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this single citation claim.

OpenEval evaluates claims C98-C99 regarding subject ages, finding them SUPPORTED as essential methodological information with appropriate age ranges. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
